approved_text: Let γ be the standard Gaussian product measure on real sequences ℕ → ℝ. Is it true that every compact balanced set K (λK ⊆ K whenever |λ| ≤ 1) with γ(K) ≥ 0.99 satisfies: 10K contains a compact convex set C with γ(C) ≥ 0.01?
draft: Let γ be the standard Gaussian product measure on the space of real sequences ℕ → ℝ. Is it true that for every compact balanced set K (λK ⊆ K whenever |λ| ≤ 1) with γ(K) ≥ 0.99, there is a compact convex set C ⊆ 10K with γ(C) ≥ 0.01?
source_docstrings:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a balanced compact set (that is, $\lambda K \subseteq K$ whenever
$|\lambda| \leq 1$) and suppose that the normalised Gaussian measure $\gamma_n(K) \geq 0.99$.
Does $10K$ contain a compact convex set $C$ with $\gamma_n(C) \geq 0.01$?
source_lean:
theorem green_54 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ K : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact K → Balanced ℝ K → (0.99 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤
    gaussianMeasureInf K → ∃ C : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact C ∧ Convex ℝ C ∧ C ⊆ (10 : ℝ) • K ∧
    (0.01 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ gaussianMeasureInf C
